questions.question: Which fields and severity values are required for every rule loaded by Engine?
options: Only name and a boolean must field
A numeric score and a model ID
name, explanation, must, and severity in low/medium/high
A regex string and a fixed priority from 1 to 10
questions.explanation: Engine validates that each rule has name, explanation, and must, and that severity belongs to SEVERITY_ORDER = (low, medium, high). Optional applies_when and fix fields add behavior but do not replace these requirements.

questions.question: What RuleResult status is emitted when a rule's applies_when predicate is false?
options: violation, because non-applicable rules fail by default
error, because every rule must apply to every response
pass, with a fabricated matched span
not_applicable, without evaluating the rule's must predicate
questions.explanation: Engine evaluates applies_when first. A false predicate creates not_applicable and skips must; it is neither a pass nor a violation.

questions.question: How does _eval_predicate combine an all_of list when one child fails?
options: It returns false immediately with that child's failing span
It returns true if any child succeeds
It evaluates only the final child in the list
It turns the list into a regular expression
questions.explanation: all_of requires every child to pass. The implementation stops at the first false child and returns its boolean and matched-span information; only after all pass does it return true.

questions.question: What happens to a text longer than the bounded-length rule's max_words=800 predicate?
options: It is automatically truncated before evaluation
The rule produces a violation with the over-limit word-count span
The rule becomes not_applicable for long text
The engine raises a parser error instead of a RuleResult
questions.explanation: max_words compares _word_count(text) to 800. A count above the limit fails the predicate and records a violation whose matched_span describes the word count.

questions.question: When does Fixer apply an append_if_missing repair?
options: On every rule evaluation, even when the rule passed
Only when the violation has no rule name
When that named rule has a fix and its stripped suffix is not already in the text
Only after replacing every regex in the constitution
questions.explanation: Fixer maps violations to rules with fixes. For append_if_missing it checks the stripped suffix first, then appends it to the stripped output only when it is absent.

questions.question: Which change operations can diff emit for a replaced line block?
options: Only one replace operation containing both versions
A JSON Patch add operation with no text
Only remove, because revised lines are not stored
edit-removed entries for old lines and edit-added entries for new lines
questions.explanation: For a SequenceMatcher replace opcode, diff records each old line as edit-removed and each new line as edit-added, preserving both sides of the reviewable change.
